new_jobs.description:
Job Number: R0251525

All-Source Intelligence Analyst, Mid

The Opportunity:

With all the information available today, it takes a skilled intelligence analyst to know how to find and interpret the best data to give their clients the right answers. With the critical decisions made in our military every day, we need an intel analyst like you to do just that. As an intelligence analyst, you use your specialized regional and functional experience and attention to detail to develop intelligence reports to give your client the actionable intelligence and context they need. If you have strong analytical skills and a problem-solving mindset, we have an opportunity to use those skills to support our warfighters.

As an intelligence analyst on our team, you’ll help your client understand the operational environment. Using your understanding of various collection platforms, you’ll explore new data sources, develop effective queries, and combine information from disparate sources, including SIGINT, GEOINT, OSINT, MASINT, and open source. The Opportunity:

With all of the information available today, it takes a skilled all-source analyst to know how to find and interpret the best data to give their clients the right answers. With the critical decisions made in our government and military every day, we need an intelligence analyst like you to do just that. new_jobs.title: Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Program Manager

Diraq is building the technology needed to make utility-scale quantum computing a reality. We’re expanding into the UK and looking for a Program Manager to join us as one of our first UK hires to lead delivery of a major, multi-year quantum computing program.
This is a role for someone who is comfortable working in an environment that is still evolving. Our technical teams are delivering complex research and engineering programs, and as we grow, we need better visibility across schedules, dependencies, risks and resources.
Your role will be to bring the right level of structure to that environment. You’ll help teams plan, identify problems earlier and make better decisions, without adding unnecessary process that slows down research and development.
Adaptability is important. Our UK operation is new, some processes are still being established, and the way we work will continue to change as the team grows. You’ll need to be comfortable working with ambiguity, making progress without everything being mapped out for you, and creating practical solutions when a process does not yet exist.  You'll be as happy to lend a hand to get things done as we stand up our UK premises as you are doing your day job.  Part of being in a scale-up means you're expected to happily work outside your core job remit and pitch in where reasonably needed.
If you need established structures and a highly predictable environment to do your best work, Diraq probably won’t be the right fit.
Working arrangement will be fully remote while we establish our UK premises - likely in Cambridge.  The role will move to a hybrid arrangement once our premises is in place.
How you work matters as much as what you deliver. We expect people to work collaboratively, treat others with respect and share credit.

Skills & Experience

Experience working in a growing or changing organisation, with the adaptability to work effectively as structures, processes and priorities evolve.
Strong program controls experience, with the judgement to know what level of control is useful and when additional process will get in the way of delivery.
Experience delivering complex programs in deep technology, hardware, semiconductors, aerospace, defence or another systems-intensive environment.
Strong program planning skills across schedules, milestones, dependencies, critical paths, resources and risks.
Experience working across technical and non-technical teams, including researchers, engineers, operations teams and senior leaders.
A relevant qualification in business, engineering, science, technology, project management or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience. Program or project management certification such as MSP, PgMP or PMP would be useful but is not essential.

Note:
Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK. Visa or work permit sponsorship is not available for this role.
This role involves access to technology subject to export controls in the United States, Australia and the United Kingdom. Applicants must be eligible to access it under those rules, which may depend on citizenship, residency, or obtaining a licence, permit or security clearance.

What you will do

Build and maintain an integrated view of program milestones, dependencies, critical paths, resources and delivery risks.
Establish practical program controls that improve visibility and predictability without creating unnecessary process.
Identify program risks and issues early, establish clear ownership and mitigation plans, and escalate blockers where needed.
Run regular cross-functional program reviews focused on decisions, blockers, dependencies and delivery priorities.
Work closely with technical program managers, research, engineering, systems engineering, operations and external partners.
Provide clear program reporting that helps senior leaders, funders and customers understand progress, risks and decisions required.
Help develop Diraq’s program management approach as our UK team and broader organisation grow.

Job Benefits

Opportunity to be involved in frontier technology that can change the world
See your impact as one of the foundational UK team
As we scale you will have a chance to grow your career

This role will initially be employed through an Employer of Record provider in the UK, with statutory UK employment benefits provided through that arrangement.

You will work with internal teams to resolve issues, communicate clear updates to partners and help ensure a smooth experience throughout the life of each agreement.

Based in London, you will work with colleagues across different regions and functions to keep licensing activities organised, ensure key obligations and deadlines are tracked, and provide ongoing support to both the team and its label partners.

Responsibilities
- Support the end-to-end licensing lifecycle, from deal initiation through to execution, onboarding and ongoing administration.
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date contract records, deal trackers, playbooks, partner information and department resources to improve consistency and efficiency across the team.
- Prepare regular updates on upcoming contractual milestones, renewals, deadlines and deliverables to support team planning and decision-making.
- Act as the day-to-day point of contact for label partners on advertising credits, as well as related advertising-account enquiries, helping them understand available balances, usage requirements and relevant deadlines.
- Coordinate partner onboarding and access to advertising accounts, working with relevant internal teams to ensure accounts and allocations are set up correctly.
- Partner with Legal, Finance, Tax, Product and Reporting teams to manage dependencies, resolve operational issues and ensure timely follow-through on partner commitments.
